source_snapshot.test_set: Intel GNR CPU RAS - Memory Demand and Patrol Scrub
source_snapshot.procedure: Configure the extensive Intel reference CScripts/ELog/WHEA/error-injection/firmware-first BIOS matrix; enable Patrol Scrub at end of POST with interval1 and DDR5 ECS, disable PTRR; verify scrubctl/en_patspr and cleared machine-check/retry registers; halt, reset injector lock and inject CE at 0x8000 with `PatrolConsume=True`; inspect MSCOD and retry_rd_err_log; resume and check serial handling.
source_snapshot.criteria: An ELog record indicated by `extlog_mem_event` is generated.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; correctly identifies the Intel harness and critical injection risk, but its truncated dmesg/SEL collection omits the source register path and explicit extlog_mem_event evidence and uses insecure SSH.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: RPUC/CHANGED with CRITICAL risk; restores target, register, extlog and BIOS-setting cleanup gates and treats the vendor harness as a prerequisite rather than intrinsic BLOCKED.
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 3. The following BIOS settings paths are from the Intel reference platform. Locations of these settings may be different on your BIOS implementation Customer Scripts (CScripts) Enabling The following is a quick reference of the key BIOS knobs for CScripts: • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > Lock Chipset = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > MSR Lock Control = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > IIO Configuration > DFX Global Configuration > — EV DFX Features = Enable — Disable BIOS Done = [X] ELOG Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > eMCA Settings > — EMCA Error Support= Enable — EMCA Logging Support= Enable — Corrected Error eLog = Enable — Memory Error eLog = Enable — Processor Error eLog = Enable Error Reporting Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > WHEA Settings > — WHEA Support = Enable — WHEA Log Memory Error = Enable — WHEA Log Processor Error = Enable — WHEA Log PCI Error = Enable Error Injection Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > — System Errors = Enable — System Memory Poison = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Error Injection Settings > — MCA Bank Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Action Table = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > — IIO/PCH Global Error Support = Enable — IIO MCA Support = Disable — IIO eDPC Support = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe* Corrected Error Threshold Counter = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe AER Corrected Errors = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > LMCE Support = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > Memory Corrected Error = Enable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Uncore Configuration > Uncore General Configuration > Directory Mode Enable = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > Enable DAM Pin = Enable Firmware First Model • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > — EMCA Logging Support = Enable — EMCA CMCI-SMI Morphing = EMCA gen2 CSMI — EMCA CMCI-SMI Threshold = 0 — EMCA MCA-SMI Enable = EMCA gen 2 - MSMI • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > OS Native AER Support = Disable Crash Log • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > CPU CrashLog Feature = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > PCH CrashLog Feature = Disable 4. Other OS Notes You can use grub2-mkconfig to specify "ras=cec_disable" by modifying /etc/default/grub's "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" with "ras=cec_disable". 【During Test】 1. Patrol Scrub specific BIOS setup : EDKII > Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > Memory RAS Configuration > — Patrol Scrub = Enable at End of Post — Patrol Scrub Interval = 1 — DDR5 ECS = Enable EDKII > Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > — PTRR DDR Enable = Disable 2. Ensure that patrol scrub is enabled on the DIMM that will be encountering the memory CECC error. >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mcs.chs.mcchan.scrubctl >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mcs.chs.mcchan.scrubctl.showfields() 3. Ensure that the machine check status register and retry_rd_err_logs are clear. Check that en_patspr is enabled in the corresponding DIMM location to log patrol scrub errors. >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.showsearch("mc_status_shadow") >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mcs.chs.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc2.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log[0].showfields() 4. Inject a correctable patrol scrub error. >>> halt() >>> ei.utils.resetInjectorLockCheck() >>> ei.mem.injectMemError(0x8000, errType="ce", PatrolConsume=True) 5. Review the machine check bank registers. Verify that a correctable patrol scrub error was logged in the MSCOD. >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.showsearch("mc_status_shadow") >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc2.ch0.mcchan.imc0_mc_status_shadow.showfields() 6. The retry_rd_err_log will also indicate a patrol scrub error was logged. >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc2.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log.showfields() 7. Resume the system and check the serial log that BIOS handled the error. >>> go() 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

test_case.test_name: Patrol Scrub — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Demonstrate on the intended Intel GNR DIMM that an injected correctable memory error is consumed by Patrol Scrub and produces the expected firmware-first machine-check, retry-read and ELog `extlog_mem_event` evidence without escalating unexpectedly.
required_package: Intel GNR SUT/CPU stepping, BIOS/BMC/OS versions and exact socket/IMC/channel/DIMM PN/serial/slot topology
Approved CScripts/error-injection package version/hash/license and supported command semantics
Project BIOS paths/values corresponding to every source reference knob plus required reboots and restoration baseline
Meaning and safe target mapping of address 0x8000, `PatrolConsume=True`, mc2/ch0 and en_patspr
Expected scrubctl fields, correctable MSCOD, retry_rd_err_log fields and extlog_mem_event/FTrace/serial/SEL correlation
Dedicated maintenance window, workload isolation, halt/go timeout, crash/OOB/BIOS recovery and cleanup plan
test_case.test_command: Record platform/CPU/BIOS/BMC/OS/DIMM topology and approved Intel harness; preserve baseline logs and BIOS/GRUB settings; apply and verify the exact source BIOS matrix with reboot as required; map the harness address and selected mc2/ch0/DIMM to the intended target; verify patrol scrub, interval, ECS, PTRR and en_patspr; preserve then clear only the approved MC/retry test registers; halt through CScripts, reset the injector lock, issue the literal CE PatrolConsume injection once, inspect the named shadow/MSCOD and retry logs, resume, collect serial/FTrace/ELog/extlog_mem_event/OS/BMC evidence, verify health, and restore all settings through an approved recovery plan.
test_case.expected_result: Verify that an ELog record was generated indicated by extlog_mem_event.
